body: I like, but don't quite love this one. The scent is nice, but it wears a bit thin on me. I wish it was a bit richer and lasted a bit longer. Darren Alan, who is one of my favorite perfumers/houses, has a similar scent called Devil's Share that is a good alternative and a touch darker, with cacao and tobacco in the base. If you like neo-vintage frags, check him out. His Chypre No. 1 (a loving homage to Coty Chypre), Dorian's Fougere, Fetes de Noel (inspired by Caron Nuit de Noël), Bathory, and Hekate are all fantastic. Fragrance Vault just started carrying his line and they ship internationally!

body: I had never smell Baccarat rouge 540 but I’ve heard so many women talking amazing about the perfume that I told my husband I wanted that to be my Mother’s Day gift, we went to Sacks to buy because he told me I need to try it on before and to my surprise it’s smell so light! The sales person gave it to me first in the paper sample, neither my husband or I could smell. We thought perhaps was the masks blocking the scent. The sales person then sprayed it on my wrist and told me to walk around the store and give it at least 20 minutes to settle. After 20 minutes we went outside the store so we could remove ours masks and smell it. I could smell it very very far, smell delicious but it was basically like if I had taken a shower and my wrist still had a little hint of perfume. My husband ( who owns and loves Lumière Noire) could not smell nothing! So he said for a bottle that expensive he expects more. Anyways we went home without buying it. Of course he bought me something I love foe Mother’s Day but not the perfect. Here I am still watching reviews about it trying to figure out why my experience was like that?

body:
The toughest thing about this is the perspective we bring into the discussion. The “fraghead” is probably exhausted by brands just pumping darker and darker AmberWoods into known sellers (that’s me from a taste perspective), but like you’ve said: we aren’t the audience. The perspective I’d love to hear would be from the folks that just want to buy one or two things, get the most longevity out of the juice, and live life not thinking about the artistry of the perfume. 

One of the things I appreciate about you is your willingness to leave a wish for what a perfume *could* be behind, and comment on it for what it is. Thanks for that. 

TL;DR: this isn’t for me, but neither are Sauvages or AmberWoods-stuffed flankers, though I hope lots of people get lots of enjoyment out of it!

body: So this video was made 4 years ago. I just bought Baccarat Rouge 540 a couple weeks ago…and had never heard of it the previous 4 years! I think there is a huge misconception when people say a fragrance is “oversaturated“, because when you walk around almost anywhere – unless you are in an extremely tight circle of people who wear fragrances – you don’t smell that many fragrances at all! That’s not to say people don’t wear them, but they are not so common that you should even worry about if something is overused or not. You should just get what you want, wear it and enjoy it. Life is too short and it’s a huge misnomer that almost any fragrance is overused! … OK, maybe the Green Polo bottle and Drakkar in the 80s…😅😂🤣😆

body: I just exchanged a perfume i thought I liked but soon realized that when you sample several fragrences in the department store, you only notice notice certain notes after a while and go nose blind. I did, however get a small sample to take home with me of TK no 4 and weeks later, tried it and WHOA!!! It gave everything I wanted and expected from BR 540 (I've tried both original and extrait)for a fraction of the $$$ and this is not only BEAST MODE but I don't get burnt cotton candy from it- more cherry? Way better and at a way cheaper price point. I also smelled TK no 10, and I want to get a sample of that and revisit. Lesson learned!  Get a sample and really give a fragrance a chance before making a final decision! So glad I gave the sample another go. Underrated but I'm okay with that 😂 I am actually glad I didn't buy BR 540. My man and I share this and both are addicted. I still get phantom whiffs several days and showers later 🎉 Unfortunately they were sold out of the big bottles, so I bought their travel set with 1oz perfume and 1oz hair mist. I think this will actually last a long time, because you need so little and it lasts so long! I did a spray of rhe hair mist on one arm, and the perfume on the other and its just a tiny bit lighter on the hair mist side. I will be using this as a body spray so great deal. 👍 As a 40 yr old woman, I find myself reaching for more unisex fragrances and I just ordered Le Labo Another 13, also! Love to hear your thoughts on these molecule/phermone type fragrences.

body: I had never heard of Kilian.  One day last winter, I was waiting for a table at a restaurant when I smelled the most incredible scent on the gentleman standing behind me.  I approached him, introduced myself and asked him what cologne he wearing.  He was very kind, he told me that it was Angel's Share by Kilian.  I felt like I was discovering a secret that few people knew-the scent was that intoxicating.  I went straight from dinner to Nordstroms and bought a travel-size, because everyone's body chemistry is different and as Chad points out, it is NOT cheap.  My wife loved it on me, and ever since, we have been on a voyage of discovery.  Prior to discovering Kilian, we had stuck to the mainstream-Caroline Herrera, Calvin Klein, the usual suspects.  Now we are having a wonderful time exploring the more boutique scents (I know Kilian is owned by Estee Lauder now, so it's hardly "boutique"...but you aren't going to find it in Target or Walmart...nothing wrong with those scents, but at our age we want something different). What I love most is how the scent changes with time, and on different people.  I never really noticed that before, but with these scents, it's very noticeable.  Angel's Share opened the door, but the scents designed for women are the most exciting for me.  My wife knows that she should not wear Good Girl Gone Bad or Sunkissed Goddess unless she wants me chasing her all over the house.  This is good stuff!  Thanks for the excellent review, Chad, and especially for the review of LV Imagination--I'll still try it, but I'm holding off on a full bottle.  You've earned my subscription!

Thank you so much for watching.

body:
As usual, a wonderful review. Thanks.
I have a different take on that one.
First of all, AS, Oajan and most of the gourmand vanillic family are all cloning a masterpiece - Hermes Ambre Narguile, by a one of the grandmasters of the craft, JCE.
Angel Share - A cloyingly sweet Danish cinnamon bun scent. Simple and boring for me.
Oajan - Not only cloyingly sweet(!), but also headache inducing. It also gave me red skin and burning sensation on my skin. What the hell did they blend in the bottle? It can be used as a chemical warfare. I bought a bottle blindly, and sold it a few days later (when I got the bottle I've received a sample of Carlisle with it. Ended up buying Carlisle instead. It's way sexier vanillic scent than Oajan).
These perfumes are really a very amateurish attempt at Ambre Narguile vibe. Unlike you, I do not appreciate the blend in Oajan. It has a too pungent cinnamon/spices. Not everyone can strike a perfect balance like Ellena.
Ambre Narguile is magical in the dry down. It goes in a different direction than AS and Oajan.

But the plot thickens with a twist - I've found Legion. Legion is a cheap clone perfume by Paris Corner. It clones Oajan according to PC.
However, on my skin it is closer to Ambre Narguile than to Oajan. It is a rare occasion where a clone is better than what it is cloning - It is not cloying. Less sweetness, more airy, less pungent / in your face. It's weaker in duration, but who cares. It is just so nice on my skin, and the best part - it costs around 30$.
As a rule, I don't do clones (I hardly do designers). However, every rule has its exceptions, and this rule has 2 exceptions  - Legion and Neroli Portfolio by Al Haramain.

body:
@SeldomlyOften Yes, AN is only sold in Hermes boutiques and in Galerie Lafayette, Paris (a cote Gare St. Lazare).
I am not a fan of sweet fragrances in general, and gourmands in particular.
However, AN is something else. On my skin the opening is gourmand-ish (albeit, much more refined than AS/Oajan), but the dry down is not. 
It just develops into the most wonderful delicate elegant scent. I sometimes layer it with just a smidgen of Pikovaya Dama, and the result is, for a lack of a better word, perfection.
It really depends on one's skin. Your milage may vary.
Can't you get a sample of AN ?

body:
I dont agree that dukhan is totally similar to o.g khamrah. It has the o.g khamrah smell in the background which is very much toned down in terms of sweetness.

Dukhan has some spicy smell. Its similar to the spicy smell you experience from rasasi dareej but you did not mention about it.  The overall vibe is a sweet and spicy smell balanced in the perfect way . Its quite masculine smelling but your entire review says it is totally similar to the o.g but no it's not. Its quite different from the o.g and the quality is the best out of the three. It smells richer with good projection. It will defenitely improve after maceration.

Coming to khamrah qahwa, i dont find it appealing. The coffee note is not that appealing  it smells quite synthetic. Many people around the world like it but its not something which will blow a begineers mind.

If you want to experience a roasted coffe note in high quality then try arabian tobacco from Ibrahim al qureshi.  High quality salted caramel coffee. Feels like entering into starbucks. Its on the expensive side but you get 200 ml and the quality is top notch.

body: Thank you so much, Erin! I bought the edp and got a sample of the extrait. I adore the EDP. Once I've really dived into all the loveliness of the edp and know it well, I'll try the extrait. I don't want to confuse my nose. Preliminary spritzes onto paper tell me the edp is brighter (as you say) but also more complex. To me the extrait seems heavier and more one dimensional. I can see men preferring the extrait because the vanilla sugar isn't as prominent and the woods are more up front. We will see. I love your fragrance reviews!!!

body: Hey, I just spent almost six hundred dollars on a bottle of Baccarat Rouge 540. body: I have tried a sample of both BR 540 and Extrait and was sad that I wasn't blown away with all the hype!  I actually was at Dillard's and a lady game me a sample of Thomas Kosmala No 4.*This woman KNOWS what people like..its kind of scary 😂)I decided a few weeks later to give it a shot and WHOA.... it literally gave me ALL the BR 540 HYPE I expected and more for a fraction of the price. I find it interesting than only men influencers make the connection that it's so very similar DNA. VERY Curious if you get a sample of Thomas Kosmala No 4 and do a wear test over the day and see if you also see the  resemblance? I'd love to hear your thoughts! TK no 4 is BEAST MODE. NOT office appropriate! I can still snell it over 24+ hrs, after showers and I swear I get phantom whiffs days later 😂 It's also the ONLY fragrence my bf has EVER complimented me on. So, I absolutely 💯 has to run to Dillard's yesterday and buy the travel set because they were sold out of the big bottle! I'm totally into unisex, Clean girl esthetic fragrences lately and just bought Le Labo Another 13 and Commodity Paper-. I'd love to hear your thoughts on "clean girl/freshies/and unisex" fragrences!!❤❤

Wow where do we start..Creed Cologne was made because they were losing business to clone houses..So they decided to bring this fragrance out to combat or recoup some investment..Then it hits open market at 435 dollars,  why come back with a new fragrance and charge that kind of money. If you wanted your share then price accordingly and watch profits roll in..I disagree with you in that there’s is no originality anymore..Your looking for something unique which unfortunately doesn’t exist..Why because that means only a select audience would be able to purchase due to price..So whether we like it or not clones, inspirations, copies whatever you want to call them are here to stay..It’s the only way the masses can sample unique blends..I don’t hate clone house because if you like the original , buy the original..Now when Adventus Cologne dropped 2 days later Dua’s already had an Inspiration of it out..Again if priced right not 435 we wouldn’t be having this conversation...So I will say Clone houses
Serve their purpose especially for discontinued fragrances...Ok enough of my rambling...Thank you for content

There is simply NO PERFUME OUT THERE THAT CAN COME CLOSE TO BACARAT ROUGE! It is that ONE perfume that has the same effect as that elixir perfume created by perfumist in that 2006 movie “Perfume: story of a murderer”. It has crowds swooned, like a spell, that you cannot put your finger on and cannot explain. If expensive royal rich lush class could be distilled into a fragrance it is exactly BACARAT ROUGE (the eau de parfum clear bottle!). Fresh, candy-flosslike, warm, mesmerising - it’s like magic in a bottle. If you want to smell of expensive class, buy this one. No questions asked. Save till you can afford it. And if it runs out, after a long time, save for it again!

body: I've smelled both angel share and Khamrah a decent amount. It's definitely based on it to a massive degree, but not exactly the same as the date accord and slight spiciness of Khamrah makes it smell distinctly more middle eastern. Both of them have amazing longevity but angel share definitely has more depth over time as you smell it. I have a 10mL decent of oajan as well and it's definitely more cinnamon heavy than the other two. I'm an advocate for wearing what you want when you want but I can't bring myself to wear oajan on hotter days because it feels way too pungent

body: So, Justin. How's it going? Hope you're well and all your viewers too. I just went to Macy's to sniff Sauvage Extrait. It's good. I get more of the Elixir DNA from it than I heard you say. It is different though. Anyway, long story short. I bought Extrait and Dior Homme Intense. I am liking Intense more and think that Sauvage Extrait is worthy, but not worth the $205 for it's size. I am not smelling it from 1 spray like you described, but it's still there, for sure. Your reviews are still insightful and I love that you always give more than just one side of a fragrances appeal. Thank you for all that you do. I want to get you my Brunello Cucinelli line of fragrances and have you create a review of all of them. Let me know, I have them all.

In my experience, I get noise blind to it after a couple of hours but others can smell it on me. I get wafts of it later in the day and it is present on my skin :)
I did not want to like it since it is so popular... but I do like it :) I use perfumes more for myself and enjoy the way they make me feel. Compliments are nice but they also mean that the scent is more mass appealing, and I like to smell more unique. 
I can not deny BR540 is a cult classic and started something special in the world of fragrances.

body:
I wonder what inspired the creator to use the scents he used to create this scent. Throughout my years, I've discovered that Perfume is a way to reveal our passions, our personalities & get our points across without words. It can make a lasting, first impression that people remember. Perfumes are powerful because we can associate them with events, memories, people & emotions.
 A great way to shop for perfumes is to smell coffee beans in between testing scents. The coffee beans help reset your olfactory bulbs.

body: I'm one of those few people that don't like Aventus (and haven't tried the cologne).  To me it's to aggressive almost and conservative.  I actually prefer Aventus for Her (which I got for my wife)  a lot more.  However my real favorite in this type scent genre is Marly's Layton which I feel is much more creative, interesting, and original.  Aventus seems more for a "stuffed shirt" and Layton seems more for those that like art house movies, that read a lot about a lot of different subjects, and that is always looking to improve themselves.  Should also mention that with Green Irish I like but the fact that it reminds me of my Dad and a fragrance he always wore (a long time ago) but I love (what could be flankers of it) Himalaya and Silver Mountain.  Great video.

body:
This is not sweet at all. Super musky, super ambroxany, not as much hedione. Instant crush is sweeter, more floral, has vanilla, less musk. Has about the same amount of hedione as br540. Instant crush is not as polarizing and more feminine. 

Really hard to say what I like most. Kosmala is really challenging. Super musky and super ambroxan. More sharp top citrus note, less sweet.

This only smells 50% like br540 extrait. I have that, and no I can barely say they're the same. I like br540 extrait more

It kept me busy for a while. Might be good for content having so many samples for your first impression vids.

body: Hi, so I actually think I know the more likely problem you might be having. You are spraying it on your neck and as you are constantly smelling it for an hour - your nose gets used to it. It doesn't mean others though won't be able to smell you. There isn't a great deal you can do about this besides not spray on neck but I think that is a key area. I like to spray a fair bit, neck included , and find if I spray some on clothes (not loads as it stains over time), as I move througout the day I will get whiffs of it. Hope this helps :)

Erin must travel in some pretty elite company if she is smelling it so often that it is losing its “specialness” and becoming “ordinary”!  I think you have to try these because the extrait de partum lasted literally for a week on the trial card I brought home from Neiman.  My bath smelled for days — just from the card!  So I bought the extrait and I’m so far stunned that this bottle smells so overwhelmingly of alcohol and lasts about 20 minutes on my skin.  I may have to return.  I cannot understand the reason.  

Meanwhile the Atelier Cologne was bought by L’Oreal and the Cedre Atlas and others are being discontinued.  Total bummer.

I wore Delina at work a few months ago and I had three different guys ask me what I was wearing…That was an indicator that:
a. Men like this fragrance A LOT
b. Delina is a loud and “look at me” fragrance 

Personally, I prefer Baccarat Rouge Extrait and I love to wear it often but I have never gotten much of a reaction from others the way Delina was. 
And yes, I also decided not to wear Delina again at work because I don’t want the attention it brings…

body:
Question, did you use/spray immediately after receiving your delivery of this, within a few days? Please know if you’re unfamiliar with, all these clone type companies do an outstanding job overall, however, we must remember, these companies are making clones of fragrances that are, 10 or more time more expensive and making their fragrances as great as possible with minimal dollars to work with, in order to sell us their dupes or clones, for under $30 or so. 
      Also, these companies immediately push their fragrances out the warehouse door, without giving the ideal maceration time, and allowing the numerous fragrances notes to become a symphony of wonderful complexity, so, if you are judging any fragrance, it’s best, to try it objectively initially, but tuck the bottle away in a moderate temperature location, and in the dark, for a minimum of 2, but ideally 3-4 months, to allow the fragrance to bloom into what it’s intended to be. Thank you.

If you leave for a while and come back, the scents return for a little bit.

body:
Completely agree with your post. As a man, I sometimes buy fragrances that I think may attractive to the opposite sex. Even though I may love the scent, they turn out to be a “oh that smells nice” kind of reaction. 
  I bought a decant of BR 540 a few years ago just to see what the hype was about. It’s unique for sure and it lasts forever on my skin. But would I be attracted to a women wearing this? Hell no. 
  On to Delina. This is what a feminine woman should smell like!  I would stalk a woman wearing this (not in a creepy way)!  This may sound strange but I judge woman by her ability or inability to pull off this fragrance. That’s how much I love Delina. 
  I’m thinking about buying Delina for my daughter but do I want the attraction she’ll probably get? Probably not.

body:
Eh... just got a small decant of Layton, and I'm not impressed at all. It's got two main accords going on the whole way through, and they're clashing in a way I don't care for:

Warm apple pie filling, big dose of vanilla, some cardamom
VS.
Sharp Menthol/camphor/medicinal florals

Idk how they made florals have a menthol type smell, but I don't find it pleasant at all. It was very disappointing after all the hype, but at least I just got a little bit instead of a $300 bottle.

body:
Until very recently I was cursing Delina Exclusif something rotten! And not for the reason you might think! My youngest sister, who loves Delina, "suggested" that I get her the Exclusif for her Christmas present last year. I duly obliged, and having helped me to blow the budget for December(she wasn't the only culprit!), I had nothing left in the pot to buy your fragrance. Worry not I said, I'll just wait till the end of the month and press the magic button. Pay day came, went onto Fragrance du Bois to make my most expensive blind buy ever and was hit with - SOLD OUT!! GRRRRRR!!! Sat and cursed at the computer for ages!

 Having all but given up hope of ever smelling your perfume, I was very grateful to hear that FdB are bringing it back. Really grateful for the second chance to buy your frag. 

Just one outstanding issue now. Haven't seen my sis all year now because of the coronavirus lockdown in the UK. So I haven't been able to catch even the merest whiff of her newly acquired Delina Exclusif!

Hey Justin, 

So I went to my closest department store today and went to the Dior counter and I asked if they had the extrait. So the lady sprayed it on a test strip then on my hand and I fell in love. I bought it right there lol I don’t usually buy a fragrance immediately after testing it in store but this one was an instant buy. Here in Australia it’s $283 aud.

For me it opens on a pineapple sweetness, lavender and woody then dries down to the Vietnamese oud and pretty smoky(I love oud soo much in general). Definitely not a blind buy safe fragrance but it’s amazing

body: The price is not shocking. Mediocre "meh" release costs today 150 dollars.200 dollars is usual price for fragrance. For me it is to much. I don't buy fragrance for more than 100 dollars. body: I have a difficult time smelling the original Sauvages. The ambroxan just destroys my nose and I go nose blind almost immediately. I think Elixer is ok but I was a little disappointed because there wasnt as much licorice as I wanted. Eau Forte was my favorite and the only one I owned until now. I think Sauvage Extrait is definitely worth it and would aruge that it is on par with something like Oud Zarian, but the Sauvage is actually stronger and cheaper. I absolutely love the mix of lavender and oud this one has, I definitely get that fresh meets dark scent profile. It is my favorite Sauvage so far and easily one my my top scents of the year. Unfortunately I live in North Arizona and it is way too hot to rock this during the day.

body: I've heard so much about creed aventus, I was curious enough to bind buy a 100ml bottle discounted to $315. I love the smell. It's everything described in this video. I'm just disappointed in the longevity. It doesn't seem to last as long as some of my other fragrances that I've paid much less for. For a perfume it seems much less than a cologne. It starts off very strong and fruity, then seems to evaporate. I still got compliments an hour after hitting myself with four sprays. Either I'm coming down with covid-19 and loosing my sense of smell or this bottle is severely diluted.

body:
You know, I went into this fragrance with low expectations. I am the type of person that doesn't gravitate to things just because they are popular. I very much like to go against the grain, to be stubborn lol... it took me a long time to try this, but I just couldn't resist. I heard so many amazing explanations, of what this fragrance is like. I didn't play around - I got a 3ml sample of BR540, and a 2ml sample of BR540 Extrait. I first sprayed both on papers. At first, meh. They both were nice, the extrait definitely had more presence right off the bat. I laid those fragrant papers down..went to work for the night. I came back to smell them the next morning, a fully dried down scent of deliciousness, decadence, a little sweet,  the depth, I don't know what it was about the second time I smelled these. It cast a spell. I was head over heels in love. Never in my life, have a tried a sample of a fragrance..especially at this price point, where I quickly searched for what bottle size I wanted, and planning a full bottle purchase. Never happened before Baccarat. I think I'll purchase original Baccarat first, but the Extrait will be next purchase after. Both are simply gorgeous..
Ladies, this will do a number on your confidence levels. I feel sexy, powerful, goddess level when I'm wearing this and dressed nice. Another first, with a fragrance.. plenty of perfumes out there make me feel beautiful, but this is on a level all its own..and I really can't describe what it is about it. 
This fragrance just...blows my mind. In my eyes, the HYPE is real, I will never be without it

body: WOW! Great, in-depth, review. Although I’ve seen dozens of reviews comparing these two fragrances, your overall presentation was calming. I have a full bottle of the EDP and a decant of the extrait from MFK’s wardrobe set. They are both really amazing. body: Hi, Erin!  Based on your reviews I was intrigued to try BR540!  Unfortunately we do not have any nearby stores that carry this fragrance.  I was super excited to discover that I could order a sample directly from MFK.  I received the sample and was absolutely intoxicated with this fragrance.  The sample was Amazing!  I could not get enough of this scent.  I was even more delighted to discover the very next week that Saks Fifth Avenue had a promotion on beauty and fragrance to save $50 on a purchase above $250.  I ordered the fragrance Immediately!  Unfortunately I was disappointed once my actual BR540 arrived.  The first spray smelled faintly of alcohol then then nothing at all.  I was so confused.  I did however get a couple of faint whiffs here and there later that night.  I thought maybe it was a fluke.  I have tried the fragrance 3 more times and still initially get a faint alcohol smell then turns into a medicinal smell like that of a dentist office.  I have read this in other reviews but couldn’t imagine what they meant until I smelled it myself.  After a couple of hours the heart notes do smell nice again but the fragrance is still more on the faint side opposed to the sample.  Do you have any idea why the sample and actual perfume would be so different?  I Really want the smell from the sample.  It was Delicious and Heavenly.  I’m not sure whether to keep or return.  I would be grateful for any advice.  Thanks so much!

body: Sir, I’ve never schmelt the Highly Acclaimed original, “Althair,” by Parfums de Marley, but I’ve schmelt both fragrances; Liquid Brun, and Island Vanilla Dunes, and as honestly gorgeous smelling as I’ll attest that Liquid Brun truly is, when I gave myself 4, yes 4 initial sprays from the new bottle, I was nostril-shocked, into the fullest gourmand incipient stage, followed through and gently holding onto me,throughout the continuous dry down experience. There are two or three other possible contenders I honestly would enjoy a chance in the judgment process, but next I’m simply going to invest into one of those tiny 2.5ml samples, even perhaps, investing a tad more, by purchasing a 5ml tester, and also buying or at least attempt to buy 3 different 5ml samples, that may be oh so different in either the openings, or even the long progression throughout the 3-4 hour dry down. However, as of right now, and so far, my favorite and best smelling fragrance I’m crazy about, is, my, Khadlaj’s  “Island Vanilla Dunes!” It currently (if the rating is accurate on Fragrantica), got an over rating of 4.51 out of 5 noses. 👈(my dumb humor😊) and that was from the total votes of 590 men, women, (other unknown chosen identities). It seem reasonable to me, but I’m rather biased, haha, lol (Laughing Out Loudly). I personally would give my first impression/experience (overall) a 4.95. Yes, for me it’s simply that Heavenly!❤😊

body: @stayfreshproductions in the EU Sauvage Elixir stayed stable at 130 euros since 2021, unlike in the US where rose every year. I know that prices are going up everywhere, but to be honest, if a fragrance is good, and the only flaw is the price, we should say that, expecially if they will hit 30 to 40% discounts in the holidays like sometimes happens. We are just giving feedbacks to the fragrance house. Today the focus is on Dior, tomorrow can be on idk Acqua di Giò. If they listen they listen, if they don't, they don't. At the end of the day, target audience or not, no one is forcing us to buy it, but in my view, every feedback is important

body: When i where the baccarat rouge 540 edp as well as You by Glossier i can't smell it an hour later but other people can and i get compliments and my husband can smell it. Now if i shower and change my clothes and spend sometime without it directly on me for a bit then pick up the sweater i wore earlier then i can smell it on it again so it is definitely still there but after awhile i just can't smell it. My signature fragrance for years was the dkny green apple and i got lots of compliments on that as well but i loved that i could smell it on myself all day. I never got nose blind to the green apple. Idk why. I love the 540 and You but wish i could enjoy it all day like i did the green apple.

body: I hear often (and respect the take) that Angel Share is one among several better amber boozy scents, and widely regarded as no longer the best, if it ever was. I personally love it. It's the feeling it gives me when I wear it that makes it the best to me, not the scent or presentation or compliment factor. But as a whole I totally understand your feelings on it. I also think that as time goes on and I experience more fragrances my pallet may evolve to want more from the artistry of scents, like yours. It makes me happy you at least don't think it's trash haha. I'd love to hear your take on more Killians

Something in that similar feel that id recommend looking for samples of is Stora Skuggan's Hexensalbe. More bitter proportionally but the vibe is still there i think.

body: I vividly remember me and my wife arriving @ Portofino on a beautiful Saturday morning. It was quite early, but coffee shops were ready to offer colazione, and thus we enjoyed a couple of cappuccino with croissants. Then we entered a shop across the street, a perfume shop, and after a pleasant conversation with the lady, I was gifted 2 samples of Aventus Cologne before we left. I always associate this fragrance with that beautiful vacation me and my wife had @ Cinque Terre. It's not an Amouage, it doesn't last long, it's not too complex, but it's absolutely one of my favorite perfumes ever.

body: Baccarat Rouge 540 Extrait is the only fragrance I own, I wear it every day, all year round, to any occasion there is. When I went in a niche fragrance store to smell it for the first time, I was just curious and was looking for that signature fragrance to buy. And so I smelled EDP and did not get the hype at all. I did not smell much to begin with, although it should be this intense fragrance. So, the girl who helped me suggested Extrait version and that changed the game for me. We ended up going around the shop, smelling a lot of different beautiful fragrances for at least an hour, but the Extrait stuck with me and when I kept returning and already comparing every other fragrance to it, I purchased my first bottle. Recently, I went in to repurchase it and tried the EDP again, still can hardly smell anything, does nothing for me. I feel like I am kind of addicted to it, when I run out, I miss it and run to the store to get a new one. My clothes, scarves, coats.. everything carries it. I leave a trail everywhere I go: the car seats, people's homes, hairdressers etc. I have noticed I am getting nose blind, so just one tiny, tiny spray is allowed, haha.

Quiero decir dos cosas, Senda, eres muy bueno describiendo y haciendo videos como somelier o reseñador de perfumes,  te mando un gran saludo desde Uruguay!! 

Ademas de eso:
Tengo ese perfume y quizas usar bufanda apague mucho su rendimiento? aunque siempre lo aplico en ropa ya que se que perdura por mucho mas tiempo, yo lo he sentido por dias en prendas pero la proyeccion he notado que quizas no era tan grande como esperaba. Dicho eso es un excelente y muy rico perfume, yo lo noté con un olor muy similar a un Nesquik, los de LATAM me van a entender. Es muy rico y adictivo la verdad.

body:
My opinions on it are the following: 
1. I think Dior should step away from milking the Sauvage name and put scents like this in their private collection or at least give it a new name for their mainstream collection. Elixir was already quite far from a Sauvage so they could've just given it a new name. This is, from your description, quite dark and niche leaning so why not give it a different name other than Sauvage because it does not seem to be fresh.
2. I believe this, like Elixir, is supposed to appeal to middle easterners and people like me who like ME perfumes. This does not sound like your standard western clean slightly chemical oud note, but rather a smoky burnt rubbery type oud. This is by choice and people from the middle east will probably like it.

body:
@Crackermac7 the opening can be a tad medicinal but after 10 min or so it starts to smell pr dang good. But that opening is a lil much if you're not expecting it. At first me and my roommates were saying it smelled like Cinnamon Vicks Vaporub. I saw a comment that said it smells Sweet and Fresh at the same time, and it's like a fight where sweet ends up winning, and that really was the best way to describe it. 

If you're getting it for a decent price, and you're looking for something good for the fall/winter without breaking the bank, I'd say go for it. Go in expecting a 7/8 out of 10 and not a perfect 10 like how all these guys push it.
Yeuh the opening is not good at all, but the dry down is decent. It's like a vanilla ice cream cone type of vibe

body: The rosee has a very 90’s fragrance vibe to it with those watery notes. It smells like a nice $75 floral freebie but offers nothing new.  The original Delina was the most unique, niche and groundbreaking as far as a new scent.  The Exclusif has the most expensive smelling notes in my opinion with the quality pear, rose and vanilla notes but might be a little too powdery for some people. I wear the Exclusif because I am obsessed with how it makes me feel but would not expect most people to feel the same.

body:
I’ve used them all as well. I started with the EDT and it’s so clean and fresh, it’ll always be towards the top of my list. EDP falls right behind the EDT for me, and Parfum lags behind. 

However, the Elixir is incredible. It’s so sophisticated and complex of a fragrance. A perfect blend of spice and woody notes, complimented by the sweetness of grapefruit. It’s a perfect winter fragrance for me. To me it comes off as a more robust and complex version of Drakkar Noir.

for me is a pass just because i dont have enough occasions to wear it. it's not a daily scent and since it's powerful yes it will last this bottle for a lot a time. but still I would prefer to spend less money and buy the elixir since its more versatile and better value. having both redundant for sure.

body:
A mí me empalagan los perfumes Dulces: stronger with You, Baccarat Rouge, Sutton Place...🤢🤢🤢🤢🤢...

Pero Liquid Brun me ha conquistado!!!❤❤❤❤❤ Su Dulzor no es común. Es un dulzor equilibrado a la perfección.

Amigos, lo único que les puedo recomendar es que no piensen en los cumplidos cuando usen una fragancia. Al final es algo que está muy influenciado por otros muchos factores, y ninguna fragancia en el mundo hace que la gente vaya cayendo a tus pies como muchos reseñados venden. Al final, los cumplidos vienen en gran parte de nuestro círculo cercano y la gente no suele girarse cuando pasas para decirte lo bien que hueles, aunque lo piensen. Si te gusta una fragancia, úsala, úsala por ti y no por los demás. Para mí, es tan simple como eso.

No he probado Layton pero no es una fragancia que me interese especialmente, con Spicebomb Extreme creo que tengo este terreno cubierto ;) espero una reseña de dicha fragancia algún día Mike!

Y también me gustaría saber tu opinión de Naxos de Xerjoff si es que has tenido oportunidad de probarla, estoy valorando que sea mi primer nicho. Gracias Mike!

body:
On her horse, little Shyamala set off on an adventure, an empty bottle in her hand. She held the bridle in her left hand and the open bottle in her right as her horse galloped off. It circled and circled. It seemed she was trying to trap something inside the bottle, but the spectators all around didn't quite understand what she was trying to imprison. But the determined young girl knew what she wanted.

The children, watching this fabulous spectacle from under the snow, cried out with delight: "Mommy, she's going to make it, right?" The carousel continued its frantic spin. Young Shyamala beamed. Now she tried to capture the scents wafting around the carousel, moving her hand like waves: the smell of snow clinging to the landscape, the scent of hot drinks, cinnamon, and honey.  The smell of fresh wood in the fireplace and the scent of gingerbread. The scent of citrus and cloves. Little Shyamala is joyful and tries to take in all the smells.

Suddenly, the horse and the music stop… the spectators around the carousel await the announcement of the result. Little Shyamala gets off the horse with the help of the showman, who hoists her up under his arms. He sets the little girl down on the snow, which crunches: “But why does the snow 'crunch' when you walk on it?” she asks the showman, who nods in response. He crouches down beside her and asks, “So, little one! Did you manage to grasp anything?” The families and the squirrel nibbling on its hazelnut have gathered around her. Everyone is silent as she unscrews the cap of the bottle.  When a "clunk" is heard: "Ohhhhh!" exclaims the audience.

The little girl delicately lifts the cork and snaps it shut. She stares straight ahead. You could hear a pin drop. The crowd and the squirrel in its tree watch the little girl and await the verdict.

Little Shymala is still staring straight ahead, her eyes wide and her mouth closed. Then suddenly she breaks into a smile, but without showing her teeth: "What's the name of the horse I'm riding?" The showman straightens up and thinks, stroking his beard: "The black horse with the gold saddle and bridle is called Oajan."

Little Shymala raises her head to look straight ahead. Then she smiles, showing her teeth, and turns to her audience and says: "So, his name will be Oajan!"

 And the audience, thrilled with joy, applauded the little girl's feat: "No! Applaud my horse instead!"

Then the audience and the squirrel began to applaud the little girl again.

The music started playing again, and all the children asked the old man to let them ride the black horse with the golden saddle and bridle.

body: ​@SeldomlyOftenOAJAN is a gourmand, generous, and warm fragrance. PDM isn't the most prestigious perfume house, but I've never smelled such a high-quality blend of honey and cinnamon in a single bottle. If you had to create a perfume based on the atmosphere and scents emanating from shops, supermarkets, shopping centers, and streets during the holiday season, this would be it! And contrary to what I read in comments on this channel and elsewhere, the perfume's performance on my skin is simply incredible. It's a playful, unpretentious fragrance. It has a simple formula that makes me smile every time I smell it. Gourmand perfumes aren't usually my favorites, but I like this one more than ANGEL SHARE, which I find too sweet and a bit synthetic. I find that perfume a little heavy. And I think the cognac note isn't given enough prominence in this fragrance. What a shame.

body:
I was away for a moment, I'm glad to see this channel is growing, it is well deserved for sure.
As for the Angel's Share, I checked alternatives or similar scent profiles that you mentioned. I still like the OG more. I bought Khamrah out of curiosity and it's not doing it for me, it smells a bit cheap I have to say.
I love Oajan and I can see the similarities, although I could wear Oajan on a daily basis, Angel's Share is more a going out type of fragrance for me.
And I would recommand another alternative, again, similar scent profile, cheaper but still, the quality is here : Nirvana by Paradis des Sens. A boozy, woody and deep scent, with cinnamon, vanilla and tonka bean.
Thank you for this review :)

body:
Just now bought this alongside homme 2020 and toy boy - the packaging was honestly really impressive, although someone didn't take the time to properly seat the bottle inside so it was a little slanted in the divot lol.

I honestly LOVE this fragrance. I know people say it's overwhelmingly sweet, but I didn't really get that - it's definitely sweet, but as a guy who doesn't normally like frags that are just sweet and nothing else, I really love this. It starts off heavy on the dates and some cinnamon - the dates really stick around the whole time but it transitions IMO from cinnamon secondary to an apple secondary on the dry down. Projects like crazy and I'm addicted to it like I never could have imagined. It is absolutely incredible in this winter weather.

I don't even care that this is a clone. I've never smelled angel's share, I have no clue how this compares to that - I just really like the smell of it...and for $30/100ml, it was a very easy blind buy. It is a disservice IMO to view this only as a clone of AS. It is a fantastic fragrance  on its own.

This is not smart from Alhambra if they want to sell in the west. You can clone a fragrance. Perfectly legal. The look and feel of a bottle design is protected by intellectual property laws. If they were smart they'd just make a brown bottle in the same colors but not at all the same shape. Like make the bottle more cylindrical instead of rectangular. Granted, i'm guessing these companies from the Middle East don't care much if they get sued. Not sure. But i get that feel. But as to this the bottle is the big issue because that is the distinct Tom Ford thing. I'd guess the bottle shape is probably protected by Tom Ford. This is very close. 

Lattafa has a bunch of sub brands all under Lattafa.
They have done this for a while noe with Oud for Greatness without problem,  it would seem.

body: Good review. For me its Creed Aventus for ever. I also like Aventus Cologne, but on my skin it smells like Armani Acqua di Gio after one hour. Also original Aventus projects better on me, sometimes longevity is almost 8 hours, which is crazy for 2024 batches, but sometimes its only 4 hours, depends on weather i think. And if you love fresh fragrances, try Louis Vuitton Imagination, i think you are not gonna be disappointed. I bought it like 3 weeks ago and people in work telling me that they can smell me everywhere, which is crazy for the fresh scent 😀 also i dont pick up any synthetic smells from Imagination, which is awesome for the designer brand, so for me it equals for niche quality.

Amazing purchase.

body: @TLTGReviews  I think the problem is that most of us don't have the patience to let the perfume sit and macerate for a few weeks or so, until the scent develops and matures. It may also be that it may grow on us after a while, which is definately the case with perfume scent profiles that we're not used to using. So we end up making our decision about the perfume there and then and I think thats a shame, as we may find that if we were a bit more patient then we may end up actually really liking it.

I have the Untold version and I must say, heads turn ALL the time. Someone is always asking me what do I have on or they complimenting me on my fragrance.
3 weeks ago  at work one of my client's came in my office and commented on my fragrance.  She asked me the name and of course I didn't say UNTOLD 🤣 but I told her the original name, the first thing she said was "I'm going to buy this today "  I said ok and smile, because I knew she was going to be shocked when she found out the price.
Long story short my client has been back 3 times since that conversation and she said nothing about purchasing this fragrance,  but when she smell it on me she immediately comments on 🤔 it smells.
I knew her reason for not saying anything was the price she found made her say HELL NAWLLLLl. 😄🤣🤣

i own all three, and my most used one nearly daily is Aventus Cologne. it projects so heavily and easily lasts me 10 hours. Mine’s an F batch and oh boy do those bad boys last. I have have an F batch of regular Aventus which i love, but i mostly wear it out on date nights 

Aventus Absolu i wore when i received my bachelors in healthcare (:

I haven't tried Creed Aventus but bought the other two based solely on your recommendation, plus Spicebomb (I used Alien Man as my main before). Bleu de Chanel simply doesn't come close to Sauvage Elixir on my skin. Top note is very different to Elixir, and not in a good way. Middle and base notes as well as longevity are much deeper and more 'mature' in the Elixir which is now my goto fragrance. P.s. Yes I know you weren't using the Elixir in this test as it hadn't even been released. I wonder if that would have won the girls vote 🙂? Test cards won't let the base notes develop as on the skin.

body: @richardspurgeon8954  actually alot of the Vloggers I watch swear by it. I have 10 bottles of dossier, plus the original for the dupes, and they honestly smell the same. Some dossiers last long and smell better than the original brand. They are actually great to try before spending hundreds on a bottle you may not like. For instance, Tom Ford is expensive, I suggested a friend by dossier version first to see how they liked it. They never brought the Tom Ford version because the dossier smelled just like it. He worked at sephora, so he knew his fragrances. I like them. If you ever watch Peyton Marie Charles the female version of BBB. She knows her smells. In one of her previous vlogs she actually paired dossier ambry saffron( 540) dupe with the new Kilian love don't be shy and it was a banger. I tried it and loved it .

body:
Great vid. 

Quick question, what are your thoughts of Sam’s Club now carrying this cologne?-Authentic?

There's something to be said about the creation of fragrances being an art form and how you'd want to keep the DNA rare and unique and how you wouldn't go buy an AI version of the original artist's music, etc. 
But there's also something to be said about huge companies that aren't hurting for money charging 300, 400, 500 dollars for a couple tablespoons of fragrance oil. Why would I EVER pay 10x more to smell almost exactly the same and support scam artists who don't want "the brokies" smelling like their products? They did it to themselves. I'd never support a clone industry if colognes were priced reasonably. But I welcome it with open arms and am hugely grateful for it.

body: ​@dmitch2001Precioux is more accurate but you only get 55 ml of juice for around 45-50 bucks for an extrait de parfum. LE is more white floral but is still really really nice and it's an edp. The pineapple and green apple pop really nice in LE meanwhile the Fruit in Precioux feels a touch less sweet and it leans more into a caramel smoky birch aventus vibe. LE is also 100 ml for around 30-35 bucks so I'd say LE is the better buy unless you want to get closer to absolu then get Precioux. Both have insane longevity off my skin I stop counting after 8 hours.

body:
I have a love hate relationship with Layton. I’m in love with the smell but it literally makes me want to throw up. 

There are sooo many strong notes, I think it overloads my olfactory senses that makes my brain think I’ve ingested something that needs to be expelled 😂

This has NEVER happened to me before, but it’s also my first extra spicy, strong, masculine leaning fragrance with sooo many notes. I feel it never gives my senses a break, I guess it’s ‘cloying’ for me. 

To enjoy it I have to use only one spary in a handful of lotion and spread it all over my body. 

If I could do a half a spray, I would. 

Other than that, It’s a masterpiece IMO

I think of CDNIM as a Mix-and-match: Take the flawless fresh-smoky drydown and add a top note of your choice. You can combine it with something Erba-Puraesque and the citrusy top note does actually become a pineapple, but Erba Pura screws with the drydown.
Hence, my personal favorite: Mix 2 parts CDNIM and 1 part Versace Blue Jeans - turns the opening into a juicy lemon not unlike Imagination while the drydown is all CDNIM.

body:
If you like all these, then you like fresh perfumes which are pleasant but very basic. Just don't forget that every of these arabian perfumes must be held in dark for 1-3 months to reach ultimate scent because unlike western niche or designers they do not let it macerate so when you receive bottle you must spray few sprays to get in oxygen and then let it macerate in bottle. That is why they are cheap. 

Try True Word from Mason Alhambra - it is fantastic dupe for Blue Talisman - fresh clean I bought even backup bottle 

Al Dana from Lattafa Niche -- as in video, sophisticated clean, 

Moody Musk - clean, second skin scent dupe for Glossier You

Shiseido Zen - very affordable beautiful citrus - orange, grapefruit scent - alternative for Coco Madmaseil - Chanel,

Junoon Oud - from Al Haramain - dupe for Sospiro Vibrato - I have both and they are almost identical - the best summer scent you ever get

body:
Yesterday (April 26th) I received a 2ml sample from PdM himself.
 But I have to admit that I don't like the scent at all.

 Firstly.....The whole storyline is very strange and weird.  First fresh, then penetratingly sweet and finally just boring wood.
 Second.....It smells too medicinal to me.  I associate it with an ointment from the 80s.
 And in the middle part I suddenly had the kokorico from jpg in my nose... somehow chocolaty.
 Which is also the only plus point about the perfume.
 The base is virtually imperceptible, as inconspicuous as it is.  Just boring.

 Third.......It doesn't last long either.
 I put 2 sprays on the back of my hand and 2 sprays in the crook of my arm......Both were hardly noticeable after less than 30 minutes.  No joke.
 The top note was gone after 10 minutes.  From there it just got sweet and woody.

 In real life I would not spend 200€ or what the perfume costs.

 I don't understand why there is wood in fresh scents anyway.  I think that spoils every summer scent.

body: It took time of letting it mature, but Nitro Black the original, not the intense, is an amazing dupe too. Again, it took a while for it to fully mature to its peak smell and performance, but once it did, the smell is extremely good. Super juicy pineapple and not a screechy opening at all and has that beautiful smokiness and depth with the birch too. I wish the atomizer wasn't complete leaky trash (maybe just my bottle), but aside from that, it's great. I have a couple decants of  Creed Aventus, plus bottles of MB Explorer, CDNIM EDT, L'Aventure, as well as Supremacy Collectors Edition and Precieux 1 (obviously those are Aventus Absolu), but they are great too and both serve incredible purposes as well. But i just blind bought CDNIM Limited Edition because it's been talked about so much and now i feel like i might need to cop Extrait de Parfum as well. Is it worth having both or are they similar enough? I've never really been a fan of the CDNIM edt, so hoping that isn't the case with the Limited Edition.

body:
No, most of the time the clones don't smell the same, most of the time it's not even 80%. I tried enough to know it and if someone claims something else they probably never tried the real ones or just try to defend their cheap buys. 

Don't get me wrong, some clones are fine in their own ways and it's no shame if you can't afford the real one, but don't pretend you do it because they are that good,  you buy the clones because you think "well... for the price it's close enough for me". Personally, if I can't afford the real one I wouldn't buy it AND also not the clone.

And remember, the most clones only exist because other people bought the real one. Without them the fake wouldn't even exist or you wouldn't even care to buy them, especially not without a test before. The clones only have value for you because the real one is so great for you or because other people think the real one is that great.

(Btw. With "you" I mean people who buy only/mostly clones, not people with some clones between)

body: I got Detour Nior quite a while ago and its been sitting for a hot minute and still Im not sure how i feel about it. That Vicks Vapor rub smell that Layton comes with in the opening is defintely amped up in Detour Nior. Also Layton  has more quality and apparent apple/vanilla too. I also get pretty dam poor performance from Detour Nior. Its hard because they are both no doubt very similar but The quality from Layton is noticably higher (which is of course expected given the drastic price difference). Might just be me but i would no doubt recommend Detour Nior if the performance was better.

Buying expensive things more often has something to do with perceived quality then flexing name brands for status. If anything making a big deal out of wearing dupes is just as much an attempt at status flexing. Fragrances also perform over time and that profile matters even more then the initial smell. Sometimes dupes create that partially, sometimes fully, sometimes it's worth buying a dupe sometimes it just isn't. Sometimes it's because the original fragrance is unreasonably overprice, sometimes the original fragrance actually has the formula to how you like your fragrance both initially and overtime. Not everything has to be cheap, not everything has to be expensive. It's not about being fooled. If you have a fragrance budget you should buy the quality you actually deem worthy of your money. Sometimes that means buying a dupe, sometimes that means by an original. You almost certainly know you are missing out when you buy only dupes. But I suppose that do know this, wouldn't make a video trying to convince people of dupes, nor don't know this already

body: Great description of both versions. When I first bought Layton it reminded me of a powdery Thierry Mugler 'Angel' for Men on steroids. I very quickly owned both and agree with everything you say. This juice is super-powerful, and can become overwhelmingly heavy if you over apply, especially the Exclusif. I go for a spray behind each ear of the original and a half spray of the Exclusif on the front of my neck and it's a great combo thats lasts and projects all day and into the evening - defo a 10/10 on the sillage front, and it can be caught 'downwind' by other people about 10 metres away too!. I do find Exclusif too overwhelming to wear on its own. Great fragrance and defo worth owning.

body: Just got a decant in mail today. First spray immediately took me to OFG - I haven't smelled atomic rose. So I guess there is some Initio vibe here via oud for greatness OG. Unlike most folks, I don't find the rose here Jammy or syrupy. I find it more like an Rose ice cream shake - something lactonic here too. It indeed is a unique scent; I'm not sure how often I'll wear this but I don't want to give it away either. Smells modern and expensive. Frankly, I was underwhelmed by OFGreatness for it's price, but this one is kinda positive surprise. It's unique.

Ho confrontato le note olfattive del Delina  parfum originale con  quelle dei profumi arabi ( riprodotti) e  qualcosa cambia , ma di poco.
L'originale possiede ambroxan che è  una nota sintetica e le riproduzioni non l'ho posseggono ed è meglio. 

In più la riproduzione di Delina viene composta aggiungendo  qualche nota olfattiva che  distingue il Delina  dal Delina la rosee.  Il vetiver l'ho rende acquatico e veramente bello.
 Possono essere profumi un pochino meno persistenti senza l ' ambroxan , ma n'è vale la pena provare. .

body:
A tip I saw somewhere to extend the cologne/perfume is using getting a small jar/container, put in a scent-free lotion, give a few sprays and mix/shake. Add more sprays if you want the smell to be stronger. 
This extends the perfume use, and the smell lasts much longer. 
For a cheaper lotion alternative, those wheat, weak sweet scented ones also work. 
The more minty lotions work with the more musky smells (not always, so mix and check, varies by ingredients used on both).

body:
Just got it yesterday, so it didn't macerate yet. Tested it at the office with my work buddies. Mixed reviews, a lot of them enjoyed the scent but found it pretty feminine, one of the girls said she wants one too so yeah I guess it is leaning on the feminine side, not what I hoped for. 

But I personally enjoy it, I'm the type of dude that likes standing out and I don't think people will find any guys smelling like this too often, this frag is close to the border between unisex and feminine for me.

The opening smells to me like new rubber, you know when you get in those auto shops that have tires and stuff, it smells just like that, like new rubber, then after a few minutes it combines that smell with roses and vanilla and stays like that for, I would say 4-5 hours after which it becomes a sweet skin scent.

I really wanna see how it develops after some maceration time, but if it becomes any sweeter, I might have to give this one to my mother, I would not want to give the impression that some lady is around and then for them to find out  that it's me who's wearing the fragrance lol

The opening smells to me like new rubber, you know when you get in those auto shops that have tires and stuff, it smells just like that, like new rubber, then after a few minutes it combines that smell with roses and vanilla and stays like that for, I would say 4-5 hours after which it becomes a sweet skin scent.

I really wanna see how it develops after some maceration time, but if it becomes any sweeter, I might have to give this one to my mother, I would not want to give the impression that some lady is around and then for them to find out  that it's me who's wearing the fragrance lol", "updatedAt": "2025-04-26T12:10:52Z", "videoId": "HS_YHabwTC4", "viewerRating": "none"}

body:
Yeah, I'm not surprised regarding the scores. Although it looks like you have an older batch with prominent menthol note. 

I have 2023 batch and unfortunately menthol note basically does not exist in comparison with the tester I smelled in the store.


It's definitely not a beast mode fragrance, at least my batch on my skin.


It's kinda sweet but not too sweet, it's kinda spicy but not too spicy, it's kinda fruity (red apple) but mainly in the opening.

I wish my bottle have this menthol note. Without that it seems to be characterless based on what I wrote before.

The overall vibe I'm getting from Layton is that is smells like apple pie. But it's sweet in a bland/characterless way.

Probably going to sell my bottle, I prefer Le Male Elixir, and I'm saying this as a person who leans towards fresh fragrances.

If you didn't like menthol note in older batches, you will be satisfied it's gone now.

You definitely can't judge a book by it's cover especially a clone by it's bottle or you will miss out on some phenomenal frags and that's FACTS!!

body: My favorite Aventus was sometime around 2014-2015, I bought a “Lot” of samples and there were two Dabber style carded samples in it one Aventus and one Green Irish Tweed. You could literally pull the rubbery dabber top out and the fragrance that was caught in it would squeeze out one good drop onto your skin and you could smell it for Hours and Hours. The G.I.T was so masculine and GREEN like Irish Spring but way fresher and Piney and mossy. Today it smells nothing like it. The Aventus was the most interesting and quality I’d ever smelled. It was really clean Musky zesty pineapple and leathery and Smoky and what I would to this day be the Best fragrances I’d smelled in my life. Since then I’ve gotten to smell other things that are great to but I have not since those 4mils of juice smelled what Clint Eastwood and James Bond wore as signature scents if anyone comes across those old glass fibber style samples GET THEM. Whatever batches those were were way better than anything that is supposed to be the same juice or clone.

body:
Thanks for the honest review. I was really hoping they would nail a summertime fresh Khamrah but it looks like other options would be  better summertime wear which in a way makes a lot of sense. Of course I probably will still pick it up when I can find it for $25-30 since I have all the line so far. 

Khamrah Qahwa so far is my favorite Knamrah since I liked the OG but it was one my wife has also worn. The coffee note really helped move it more in a slightly more masculine way. Dukhan is nice and moves the needle a bit more masculine but when you have been rocking Khamara Qahwa for a year (when seasonally appropriate) the compliments for Dukhan just don’t come as often.
Nice

body: Branding is mainly what makes it absurdly expensive, the reason why it should be expensive is because of natural or absolute extraction from plant material that were used and the nose behind the composition, most clones do exceptionally well on longevity of the perfume and near overall scent profile but can not fully capture how the perfume smells over time and its niche quality. It still smells great but is cheap because its more synthetic in its composition, aroma-chemicals are cost effective and important in perfume backbone structure, however can smell linear and sharp without natural materials. Lattafa and Armaf does a great job capturing their original characteristics at a cost-effective price and is not a scam which i highly support, its great for people who simply want to smell nice except those that freak about smelling like everyone else.

body: As it should. Designers are pulling in around 90% of their sales in profit. Armaf can charge €25 for a perfume and still be a very successful company. Perfume oil isn't expensive at all, and doesn't take a rocket scientist to make a mass appealing perfume. The creed brothers aren't making cdni, but it's still a good perfume. €130 for 100ml of the newest designer is insanity. We all laughed at chanel when they charged this for bleu while versace were charging €80 for eros. Now €130 has become the standard. These "elixers" are selling for €200+ a myself and svauge flanker for €200?? Get a grip. I'm going with clones, all I want is to be smell nice when people get within 2 feet of me. Don't need to spend €200 for that. If you have the money to spend then absolutely go for it, but clone houses are putting their customers first and they deserve the success they receive ❤

body:
I have purchased a number of designer fragrances and their clones. Clones can be very hit or miss. So before you go blind buying every lattafa I would suggest doing research.
Frankly to my nose, I have disliked most of my Lattafa perfumes. Designer fragrances are blended perfectly versus subtle inadequacies in cheaper scents.

Clones CAN get the scent profile very close to designer- but at the end of the day it will not be the same thing, and usually does not blend as organically as designer scent profiles do.

body:
I remember my sis bought me a fragrance, it was my first, I wasn't that knowledgeable. I don't even remember it's name, ngl. But it lasted me like 2-3 years. I did like 2-3 times before going to school. 
Everyone kept asking me "dayum, is that one million I'm smelling" or something like that. I knew it wasn't one million, well because the box said other brand(?) name. So it felt weird. By saying "no" they would've mocked me for being poor. 
Years later I bought the one million, since now I can afford that, and to be fair, they really smelled alike. From now on I'll probably buy the clones and pretend I'm using the real deal.

body:
Thanks for the video. I'm wearing Layton as I watch this. I'm always curious when you do these tests: How soon after spraying the test strip do you let people smell it? In other words, are they only getting the opening of the fragrance, or the mid, or the base? Maybe in future videos, you can have one that has the dry down and one that has the opening so they could see how it ends unless it's a linear fragrance.

In all actuality, unless it's a very linear scent, by the time you meet up with the girl on a date or you get to the office, you're going to be past the opening stage anyway, unless you're applying it right before meeting up.

Judging a perfume by its opening is like judging a book by its cover: pointless and irrelevant.

I totally get your point and share the same thoughts!
Afnan 9pm smells like cough medicine in the opening. The drydown reminds me of the og Le Male.

body: Honestly I do sort of disagree I think this would smell much better on a woman than a man but I think it smells soo good I still will wear it come winter it’s just lacking a certain element that a guy would need. I do however feel myself leaning usually towards unisex and also sometimes feminine fragrances so I don’t really mind. I have an oud oil which is also rose but has lavender and jasmine with a really strong oud that adds that masculine power element I would say that’s the perfect mix but the rose is so much louder in amethyst maybe I’ll mix the two or mix amethyst with a leather perfume , regardless it smells amazing and If ur someone who likes unisex sort of feminine leaning scents and doesn’t really care you’ll like it it’s not really for fresh manly scent lovers though. But honestly for 30$ try it out ! If you don’t like it you can always pass it on to a woman in your life

body:
I really don't care for the menthol / Vick's Vapor Rub opening of Parfums de Marly LAYTON.   I was inspired to experiment a bit, to see if I could find a way to decrease (or remove) the strong "Vicks" smell from a bottle of Layton (or a clone version like Detour Noir, Northstag Expressions - Deux or The Woods Collection - Dusk)

After watching dozens of cologne videos and shorts, I came up with a plan.   I spent a couple weeks mixing and blending fragrances like a mad scientist.  My final version used 70% Layton, and I added about 15% additional Citrus/Orange (a mixture of Odyssey Mandarin Sky 20% + L.V. Orage 80%).  I also added 15% of a vanilla heavy fragrance (Khadlaj Empire Victor).  It worked!  I now have a beautiful, almost menthol free LAYTON.  

Ok, I realize that I probably shouldn't call my version LAYTON because the menthol is an important part of the fragrance and I've severely altered that aspect.  So, let's just say I have a beautiful, classy cologne that doesn't get me complaints like:  "HEY, WHO'S WEARING VICKS?!  I HATE THE SMELL OF VICKS.  WHO PUT VICKS ON?!?!"

(I left out the boring, lengthy discussion describing my dozens of experiments that led me to my 70%, 15% + 15% final version.)

Could somebody offer their expert perfumer's analysis as to why my three additional ingredients almost completely wiped out the menthol?  I think I just got lucky, but I'd love to know the actual chemistry involved.   Thanks.

body:
HERE'S A FOLLOW UP:

I came across this info on the internet and it seems to match what I discovered empirically in my Layton journey:

"Perfumers typically use a high ratio of citrus to menthol (often 4:1).  Overdosing menthol can lead to a harsh, medicinal, or "chemical" smell that overpowers the fruit."

Dare I say that PDM Layton has just a touch too much menthol?  I'm totally guessing... maybe 3:1 or 2:1???  And thus, when I added lemon, grapefruit, and orange it changed this ratio... which diminished the strength of the menthol. (It was a lucky guess I made during my experiments.)

Another nice tidbit of info that I came across:

"The sweetness of orange can soften the biting coldness of menthol, creating a smoother profile."

Ok, so not only did my orange mixture add sweetness, but the vanilla I added also contributed to sweetness / smoothness.

I'm very happy with the mad-scientist Layton blend I ended up with.  It's been a fun journey.

I have discovered that I can apply this citrus/orange/vanilla modification to one of the highest Vicks menthol versions of Layton that I've come across:  Al Haramain DETOUR NOIR, and I still get the reduction in menthol that I am looking for.  That's perfect!  It becomes an apple / mandarin orange / vanilla / slightly woody cologne.

body: Really enjoyed the video! Personally, I love Layton, and own a full bottle; scent is such a personal and subjective thing, so always take reactions with a grain of salt, please. Also, testing a scent on paper is just a horrible representation of what a fragrance actually is, which, unfortunately, is one of the only ways you can get street reactions without sticking your arm/neck in someone's face. Everyone who is actually interested in Layton, please buy a small sample for $10-$20 (2ml-5ml is plenty) and test it on your skin. That "medicinal" opening doesn't happen for me, but I can see how people interpret it that way; anyway, that opening lasts all of ninety seconds, so it's honestly a moot point, IMO. After two minutes, you get a sweet apple, floral vanilla, and then after fifteen minutes or so it melts in to the spicy sweet drydown, which is linear, but smells incredible, and lasts ten or more hours. THAT is why this fragrance is hyped. Doing a street reaction in 32F/1C weather, smelling something off a piece of paper, is not going to do ANY fragrance justice.

I know this might just be me. 

Made the mistake of blind buying this one. It's so bad. Smells rotten. No matter how much I tried to wash it of, it just sticks to my skin. The sweet puke-ish smell is making me gag. 

I went to a store that had more Lattafa and tried to smell some of the other offers. All of them, like literally all of them had the exact same undertone of something thick, rotten, puke-ish. Maybe I just don't like Arab fragrances, or Lattafa is bad and everyone is roleplaying to like them. 
The smell even sticks to the inside of my nose, and I could not get rid of the horrible smell.

body:
I definitely agree PDM Percival would get better ratings bcause people in the fragrance community always underestimate how lay people love fresh and clean fragrances, 

Great description of Layton btw. Concerning Layton it smells quality but yes you can smell something synthetic at the opening, Naxos from Xerjoff has a similar effect where the opening is agressive but the dry down is lovely for both fragrances.

Percival would prolly win, as fresh scents tend to be more mass appealing. But Layton is a better smell. I don't rely get the dad comments tbh, I don't think it smells like something an old person would wear, but that might just be because it actually smells like quality and younger guys rarely wear niche scents

body: I happen to have the Aventus Absolu. I accidentally layered it with Aventus OG F batch. This happened when I used a decant to recharge the OG. The results were impressive combining the silage and light fruity scent of the OG with the deep complex longevity of the Absolu. If you happen to have both, give it a shot. Also, I have a sample of the first Absolu released a couple of years ago. And yes, I can see a similarity to the Sauvage Elixir at the dry down. However, the full bottle I have now is the current release. This one at dry down is less like the Sauvage elixir compared to the first one. Other than that, they are pretty close. The latest release is not being reviewed much on YouTube.

It was the scent I wore the day my son was born.

I can't imagine a cheap perfume evolves as much as greenly, greenly is one of the most complex perfumes I've ever smelled, even though it just smells like green soap 😂 if aether has that opening and kinda drys down like any other cheapy then I'd defo consider it. But if the deep dry down is the same as greenly I'd have to pass. Just too weird and green for me

Don't even bother with clones, they are made with cheap materials and don't smell anywhere close to what they're supposed clone is from. Spend the extra $50-$100 for a real brand cologne. 

Got a oud wood tom ford clone from jomas or whatever site , and it fkin sux. Not even worth 30$ 

You get what you pay for and I personally have had good feedback from real Hugo boss cologne or even real tom for EDT dont come off strong and smell way nicer than any clones. 

Just thought I'd say it after the disappointing experience with these clones suggestions. 

Maybe I'll find a clone of the Hugo boss one I got good feedback on and see what the consensus is but the issue is the solvent used not being an expensive one and you risk giving people around you a headache 🤣
